registered: 2026-11-18 ~12:15 ET, before any signal was joined to its earlier same-day signals
operator: 11/18: 'How can we know the performance of the name prior to buying it for the first time?' ... 'Yes, test it'
question: Does the outcome of a name's EARLIER pre-square signal today (taken or not) predict its next one?
data: the desk's live pre-square arm on SIP minute bars (news_source.signals_for: fast %R 21, refractory 30, minutes 15-360), top-400 universe, every warehouse day with SPY. The CURRENT signal must pass the BASE admission ($20-$400, up >= 1.5%); earlier signals count whatever their admission (price band only). Trade: open t+1 -> close t+10, 6 bp.
no_lookahead: an earlier signal counts only if its 10-minute outcome is complete before the current signal minute (t_prev + 10 < t; the 30-min refractory guarantees it)

groups.WIN: the most recent earlier signal today netted > 0
groups.NONE: no earlier signal today (information: confounded with time of day)

statistic: per day with both groups: mean WIN - mean LOSS (bp); day-clustered t

pass_if_ALL.both_halves: WIN - LOSS > 0 in the first and second half of the days
pass_if_ALL.win_beats_all: WIN mean > mean of all current signals

information: NONE vs WIN vs LOSS by time of day
straight-down share (low over t+1..t+10 <= open - 40 bp) per group
mean of all earlier signals today instead of the last one
after_pass: a live feature: for each name, the outcome of its last pre-square signal today from the desk's own bars; use for first-trade sizing (full size after a working earlier signal, reduced otherwise) or slot priority - built behind a switch, ships (paper) under the operator's 11/18 rule
else: record; the first trade stays at half size (row 147)
caveats: minute bars with a fixed 10-minute exit; LOSS includes signals that only lost the 6 bp cost
